name: Rubbish to Riches!

pick.label: Pick some rubbish
pick.heading: Pick something people throw away and make it into a product
lead: Every day, Berlin throws away mountains of stuff that still has some life in it. Some designers have built whole brands out of other people’s rubbish: bags from old lorry covers, trainers from old seat fabric, furniture from old pallets.
Choose something from the shelf (or your own idea) and turn it into a product people would actually pay for. *The sillier the rubbish, the better.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: This is not a business plan, it’s just for a bit of fun. Some ideas will make total sense, and some will only make sense to you. Both are welcome.

shelf.head: From the street
items: E-scooters fished out of the Spree

rows: What are you rescuing from the bin?
What exactly is the product? A bag, a lamp, a snack, something completely mad?
Colours, finish, size, smell… What does it look like in the shop?
Who buys it first? Students, tourists, your grandmother, someone else?
How much, and why is it worth it?
Where is it sold, and who do you get to talk about it?

values.rubbish: Tents that people leave behind after music festivals.
values.product: The Morning After: a raincoat made from an abandoned festival tent. Every coat still has the tent’s pockets, and some still have a bit of glitter you will never get out.
values.look: Bright and a bit crumpled, with a matt finish, and a few of them still smell faintly of cider.
values.who: People who go to festivals and forget to pack a jacket, which, in my experience, is everyone.
values.price: €89, which is more than the tent cost, but the tent didn’t come with a story.
values.promote: A stand at the same festival the next summer, so people can buy back their own tent as a coat. In the Scottish rain, it sells itself.
